questions.question: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (MPI) was released by which of the following?
questions.questionHtml: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (MPI) was released by which of the following?

options.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
options.html: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is NITl Aayog.

Key Points

  • National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (MPI):-
    • It is a comprehensive measure of poverty that captures multiple deprivations faced by households across the three macro dimensions of health, education, and living standards.
    • It is the first-of-its-kind index developed for India, and it is based on the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) data.
    • It was released by NITI Aayog.
  • NITl Aayog:-
    • NITI Aayog, also known as the National Institution for Transforming India, is a public policy think tank of the Government of India.
    • It was established with the aim of achieving sustainable development and good governance.
    • It was formed on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission of India.

Additional Information

  •  World Bank:-
    • The World Bank is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to the governments of low- and middle-income countries for the purpose of pursuing capital projects.
  • Ministry of Finance:-
    • The Ministry of Finance (MoF) is a ministry within the Government of India responsible for the economy of India, serving as the Treasury of India.
    • The MoF is headed by the Minister of Finance, who is a member of the Cabinet of India. 
  • Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:-
    • It is a Government of India ministry that is responsible for welfare, social justice, and empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society.
    • These sections include Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), persons with disabilities, minorities, and victims of atrocities. 
    • The MSJE is headed by a Cabinet minister and assisted by two Ministers of State.

questions.question: In which year did E Gorter and F Grendel make a breakthrough by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be of two layers?
questions.questionHtml: In which year did E Gorter and F Grendel make a breakthrough by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be of two layers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1925.

Key Points

  • Langmuir Trough Experiment:-
    • E Gorter and F Grendel made a breakthrough by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be of two layers in the year 1925.
    • Their experiment involved extracting lipids from red blood cells and then spreading them out on a water surface to form a monolayer.
    • They then measured the area of the monolayer and found that it was twice the area of the surface area of the red blood cells.
    • This led them to conclude that the lipid bilayer model of the cell membrane must be correct.
    • Gorter and Grendel's work was a major breakthrough in the understanding of cell structure and function.
    • It helped to establish the lipid bilayer model of the cell membrane, which is still the accepted model today.

questions.question: Who among the following advocated the ideology of “oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu” (one caste, one religion, one god for humankind)?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following advocated the ideology of “oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu” (one caste, one religion, one god for humankind)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Narayana Guru .

Key Points

  •  Narayana Guru:-
    • He was a great saint and social reformer of India. He preached for religious unity and social equality in Hinduism.
    • He is considered to be one of the greatest religious and social leaders of Kerala.
    • Narayana Guru gave his first sermon in 1884. He preached for religious unity and social equality in Hinduism.
    • He opposed the caste system, discrimination, and other social evils.
    • The ideology of “oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu” (one caste, one religion, one god for humankind) was advocated by Shri Narayana Guru only.

Additional Information

  • Swami Shraddhanand:-
    • He was an Arya Samaj sannyasi and an Indian Independence activist who propagated the teachings of Dayananda Saraswati.
    • He was a key figure in the Hindu Sangathan movement in the early 20th century, which aimed to unite Hindus and promote Hindu nationalism.
  • Birsa Munda:-
    • He was an Indian tribal freedom fighter and folk hero who belonged to the Munda tribe.
    • He led a tribal religious millenarian movement that arose in the Bengal Presidency (now Jharkhand) in the late 19th century, during the British Raj, thereby making him an important figure in the history of the Indian independence movement.
  • Keshub Chunder Sen:-
    • He was a Hindu philosopher and social reformer who attempted to incorporate Christian theology within the framework of Hindu thought.
    • He became a member of the Brahmo Samaj in 1857 but established his own breakaway "Bharatvarshiya Brahmo Samaj" in 1866 while the Brahmo Samaj remained under the leadership of Debendranath Tagore (who headed the Brahmo Samaj till his death in 1905).

Key Points

  •  e-Shram portal:-
    • It is a national database of unorganized workers, which was launched in August 2021.
    • It is a one-stop shop for unorganized workers to access information and services related to social security schemes.
    • The portal also provides a platform for workers to register themselves and get a Universal Account Number (UAN), which can be used to access various social security schemes.
    • As of July 2022, approximately 28.96 crore unorganized sector workers are registered on the e-Shram portal.
    • This number is constantly increasing, as the government is encouraging more and more workers to register on the portal.

    • These are those who work in enterprises that are not registered under any law or which employ less than 10 workers.
    • They are also known as informal workers. Unorganised sector workers make up the majority of the workforce in India, accounting for over 90% of all employment.

questions.question: Moplahs, or Muslim peasants, created a powerful anti-zamindar movement in:
questions.questionHtml: Moplahs, or Muslim peasants, created a powerful anti-zamindar movement in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kerala.

Key Points

  • Moplahs:-
    • The Moplahs, also known as Mappilas, are a Muslim community indigenous to the Malabar Coast of Kerala, India. 
    • They are believed to have descended from Arab traders who settled in the region in the 9th century and intermarried with the local population.
    • The Moplahs have a distinct culture and language, which is a mix of Malayalam and Arabic.
    • They were one of the leading communities in the Malabar Rebellion of 1921, which was a peasant uprising against British colonial rule and the prevailing feudal system.
    • The Moplahs have also made significant contributions to the fields of art, literature, and politics.

Additional Information

  • Moplah Rebellion of 1921:-
    • It​ was the culmination of a series of riots by Moplahs (Muslims of Malabar) in the 19th and early 20th centuries against the British and the Hindu landlords in Malabar (Northern Kerala). 
    • Most Moplahs were predominantly converted Hindus during Tipu Sultan's capture of Malabar.
    • The prominent leaders of the rebellion were Ali Musaliyar and Variyankunnath Kunjahammed Haji.
    • In November 1921, 67 Moplah prisoners were killed when they were being transported in a closed freight wagon from Tirur to the Central Prison in Podanur. They died of suffocation. This event is called Wagon Tragedy.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India incorporates the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.questionHtml: Which part of the Constitution of India incorporates the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Part IV.

Key Points

  • Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of our State Policy (DPSP)
    • It includes Articles 36-51.
    • The provisions contained in this Part cannot be enforced by any court, but these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
    • The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy was borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
    • While most of the Fundamental Rights are negative obligations on the state, DPSPs are positive obligations on the state, though not enforceable in a court of law.

    • It is the total amount of money that an individual or household receives in a given period of time, typically a year.

questions.question: An 11-digit number 7823326867X is divisible by 18. What is the value of X?
questions.questionHtml: An 11-digit number 7823326867X is divisible by 18. What is the value of X?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 18, it must be even and the sum of its digits must be divisible by 9.

Sum of digits of 7823326867X = 7 + 8 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 6 + 8 + 6 + 7 + X = 52 + X.

The nearest multiple of 9 greater than 52 is 54.

Equating: 52 + X = 54 ⇒ X = 2.

Since 2 is even, both conditions are satisfied.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given: The 11-digit number is 7823326867X and it is divisible by 18.

Divisibility Rule of 18: A number is divisible by 18 if it is divisible by both its co-prime factors, 2 and 9.

⇒ Condition 1: The number must be divisible by 2, which means the last digit X must be an even number (0, 2, 4, 6, or 8).

⇒ Condition 2: The number must be divisible by 9, which means the sum of its digits must be a multiple of 9.

⇒ Sum of digits = 7 + 8 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 6 + 8 + 6 + 7 + X

⇒ Sum = 52 + X

⇒ For (52 + X) to be divisible by 9, we check possible values of X from the options:

⇒ If X = 6, Sum = 52 + 6 = 58 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ If X = 4, Sum = 52 + 4 = 56 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ If X = 8, Sum = 52 + 8 = 60 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ If X = 2, Sum = 52 + 2 = 54 (Divisible by 9, as 9 × 6 = 54)

⇒ Since X = 2 is even, it also satisfies the divisibility rule for 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is exactly divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 2

A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number n, the number must be divisible by the co-prime factors of n (e.g., for 12, check 3 and 4; for 15, check 3 and 5).

options.html: Do you want to join us for lunch?

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: and don't finish till 3 p.m.

 Key Points

  • According to the rules of sub-verb agreement, singular subjects take singular verbs and plural subjects take plural verbs.
  • The subject and verb must agree in number: both must be singular, or both must be plural.
  • In the question, the subject of the sentence "physics class" is actually singular (as it refers to one class), but the verb "don't" is a contraction of "do not," which is plural.
  • Hence, there is a mismatch in the subject-verb agreement. With a singular subject "physics class," the verb also has to be in its singular form.
  • The correct form would be "doesn't," the contraction of "does not."

So, the corrected sentence would be: "I'm sorry, my physics class will start at 1 p.m. and doesn't finish till 3 p.m."

A. But at the same time, this is also true that when one reads a few works of the same genre, one naturally comes to know a rough structure of that genre.

B. The essence of suspense is whether the reader will be able to gauge the criminal before the detective tells who he is.

C. This leads to a different kind of approach to understanding literature in general and detective fiction in particular.

D It is found that when one knows a genre and its structure and rules, it may often not make us enjoy a piece of literary work in the same manner as one usually does.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option no. (1)  'DACB'. Key Points

  • Sentence D talks about how knowing the structure and rules of a genre may not necessarily make us enjoy a literary work in the same way.
  • Sentence A adds that reading multiple works of the same genre helps us understand its structure and rules.
  • Sentence C implies that this understanding leads to a different approach to understanding literature, specifically detective fiction.
  • Sentence B defines the essence of suspense in detective fiction.
  • The meaning arrangement of the sentences will be: It is found that when knows a genre and its structure and rules, it may often not make us enjoy a piece of literary work in the same manner as one usually does.But at the same time, this is also true that when one reads a few works of the same genre,one naturally comes to know a rough structure of that genre.This leads to a different kind of approach to understanding literature in general and detective fiction in particular.The essence of suspense is whether the reader will be able to gauge the criminal before the detective tells who he is.

Therefore,the correct answer is option no.(1)

 Additional Information

  • Option 2 (BDCA): Starts with the definition of suspense in detective fiction and then talks about how understanding the structure of the genre may affect our enjoyment of it, before ending with a vague statement about a different approach to literature. -
  • Option 3 (CBAD): Starts with a statement about understanding the structure of a genre, then jumps to how this understanding affects our enjoyment of it, before ending with a statement about a different approach to literature and detective fiction.
  •  Option 4 (ADCB): Starts with a statement about understanding the structure of a genre and how it affects our enjoyment of it, then jumps to a vague statement about a different approach to literature, before ending with the definition of suspense in detective fiction.

questions.question: Describe how you will tell your friends that someone has picked Suman’s pocket in passive voice.
questions.questionHtml: Describe how you will tell your friends that someone has picked Suman’s pocket in passive voice.

options.text: Someone has being picked Suman’s pocket.
options.html: Someone has being picked Suman’s pocket.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (4) "Suman's pocket has been picked."  Key Points

  • The sentence is in passive voice, which means the subject of given sentence will not do any work itself.
  • Instead, the focus is on the object (Suman's pocket) and the action that was done to it (picked).
  • The verb "picked" is in the past participle form, which is used in passive voice constructions.
  • It is formed by adding "-ed" to regular verbs or using the third form of irregular verbs.
  •  The auxiliary verb "has been" is used to form the present perfect passive tense. This indicates that the action happened at an unspecified time before now and has ongoing effects.
  •  In active voice, the sentence would be "Someone has picked Suman's pocket." The subject (someone) is doing the action (picking), and the object (Suman's pocket) is receiving the action.

Therefore,the correct answer is option no.(4) Additional Information

  • Option 1, "Someone has being picked Suman's pocket," is incorrect because "being" is not needed in passive voice constructions. It also uses the wrong form of the verb "pick." -
  • Option 2, "Suman's pocket had picked," is incorrect because it uses the wrong form of the verb "pick" and the wrong tense. "Had picked" is past perfect, which is used to indicate an action that was completed before another past action. -
  • Option 3, "Suman's pocket been picked," is incorrect because it is missing the auxiliary verb "has been" and the main verb "picked" is in the wrong form.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It could possibly lead to serious injuries, hence a mate for N' Pongo became inevitable.

B. Within the span of one year, N' Pongo grew double the size and the need to obtain a mate for him arose, for it becomes unsafe for the humans around.

C. Every afternoon he was brought out onto the lawn to show off his skills in front of his admirers.

D. Owing to his attractive appearance and disposition, good manners and a well- developed sense of humor, N' Pongo soon became the darling of the zoo.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option no. (1) 'DCBA'. 

Key Points

  • The paragraph talks about N' Pongo, a zoo animal who grew double in size within a year, making it unsafe for humans around him.
  • Due to this, the need to obtain a mate for him arose to avoid serious injuries.
  • N' Pongo became popular among visitors due to his attractive appearance, good manners, and sense of humor.
  • Every afternoon, he was brought out onto the lawn to showcase his skills in front of his admirers.
  • The above sentences describe the connection and meaning of the passage.
  • The complete passage will be:Owing to his attractive and disposition,good manners and a well-developed sense of humor, N'Pongo soon became the darling of the zoo.Every afternoon he was brought out onto the lawn to show off his skills in front of his admirers.Within the span of one year,N'Pongo grew doubel the size and the need to obtain a mate for him arose,for it becomes unsafe for the humans around.It could possibly need to serious injuries,hence a mate for N'Pongo became inevitable.

Therefore,the correct answer is option no. (1)

 Additional Information

  • Option 2 - DABC: The first two sentences are in the correct order, but the last two are swapped.
  • Option 3 - CDAB: The first and last sentences are swapped, and the remaining two are in the correct order.

  • Let's take a look at the phrase: This book (1) _______ writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them,
  • Let's take a look at the options:
  • The subject of the sentence is singular ("Select"), so we need a singular verb.
  • "Provides" is the correct singular form of the verb. - "Provide" is the plural form of the verb, so it would be incorrect in this sentence. -
  • "Is providing" is the present continuous tense, which suggests an ongoing action. This tense would not make sense in this context. -
  • "Had provided" is the past perfect tense, which suggests an action that was completed before another past action. This tense would also not make sense in this context.
  • Having explained the options we find 'provides' will be the most appropriate option for the given blank.
  • The complete phrase will be: This book provides writing practice to pre-schoolers to help them,

Therefore, the correct answer is option no.(1)

 Additional Information

  • Option 2, "provide", is the plural form of the verb and would not be correct with a singular subject.
  • Option 3, "is providing", suggests an ongoing action and does not fit the context of the sentence. 
  • Option 4, "had provided", suggests a completed action in the past and does not fit the context of the sentence.
